verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew safely returned to Earth on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The Artemis II crew is returning to Earth... Orion capsule is due to reenter... on Friday, April 10, 2026.'; R2: 'Artemis II's astronauts returned from the moon with a dramatic splashdown... on Friday'; R3: 'The Artemis II crew is officially home after their Orion spacecraft splashed down... on April 10, 2026.'; R4: 'SPLASHDOWN! ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT'; R5: 'Artemis II crew splashes down... April 10, 2026'; R6: 'safely home, having splashed down in the Pacific Ocean'
verifications.reasoning: All references directly confirm safe return via splashdown on April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consists of four astronauts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The four astronauts aboard'; R2: 'crew of four'; R3: 'The four astronauts'; R4: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; R5: 'crew of four astronauts'; R6: 'four-person crew'
verifications.reasoning: Every reference explicitly states the crew consists of four astronauts, often naming them.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8:07 p.m.: Splashdown in the Pacific Ocean... off the coast of San Diego, California'; R3: 'landed in the Pacific Ocean... at 8:07 p.m. ET... off the coast of California'; R4: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT'; R5: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego... at 8:07 p.m. EDT'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references precisely match location, ocean, coast of California/San Diego, and exact time.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'final day of their 10-day milestone mission'; R2: 'nearly 10-day flight'; R3: 'historic 10-day Artemis II mission'; R4: 'approximate 10-day mission'; R5: 'historic 10-day mission'; R6: '10-day journey'
verifications.reasoning: All references describe it directly as a 10-day (or nearly/approximate) mission.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission took the crew around the far side of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'mission to orbit the moon'; R2: 'lunar flyby... moon's far side — never seen before by human eyes'; R3: 'took the four astronauts around the far side of the moon'; R6: 'circled behind it... far side of the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: References explicitly state flyby/orbit around the far side of the Moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew includes the first Canadian to fly to the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Jeremy Hansen — now the first Canadian to fly to the moon'; R4: 'CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; R6: 'Jeremy Hansen, the first Canadian to go to the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Directly identifies Jeremy Hansen as the first Canadian to fly to the Moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission broke records for human distance from Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'broke Apollo 13's distance record and marked the farthest that humans have ever journeyed from Earth when the crew reached 252,756 miles'; R3: 'farther from Earth than any humans had gone before, beating the previous record set by Apollo 13'; R6: 'travelled deeper into space than ever before... 252,756 miles'
verifications.reasoning: References confirm breaking Apollo 13 record for farthest human distance from Earth.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule touched down at 8:07 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8:07 p.m.: Splashdown... April 10, 2026'; R3: 'official splashdown time of 8:07:27 p.m. ET... April 10, 2026'; R4: 'SPLASHDOWN! ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT'; R5: 'splashing down... at 8:07 p.m. EDT... April 10, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and date for Orion splashdown/touchdown confirmed in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew was reported to be in good health.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'all four crew members are safe and well... All four astronauts have made the short walk... unaided'; R4: 'safely extracted... safely aboard'; R5: 'hale and hearty... "four green crewmembers"... feeling great, happy to be home'
verifications.reasoning: Direct reports of crew being safe, well, healthy, and in good spirits post-splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew transitioned to the USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'recovery ship USS John P. Murtha awaited'; R3: 'aboard a rescue ship... USS John P. Murtha'; R4: 'safely aboard the USS John P. Murtha'; R5: 'now on the USS John P. Murtha, the recovery ship'; R6: 'flown to the USS John P Murtha'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources confirm crew transfer to USS John P. Murtha after splashdown.

verifications.claim: All systems functioned as planned on the Artemis II mission
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: 'not without technical issues. Both the capsule's drinking water and propellant systems were hit with valve problems... the toilet kept malfunctioning'; R3: 'some learning curves and issues (I’m looking at you, space toilet)'
verifications.reasoning: References explicitly mention technical issues (valves, toilet), contradicting 'all systems as planned' despite overall success.
